why: Both cover the same aggression toward a neighbour's flag, and the material constantly overlaps destroying a rival's work with growing the room's own work over its space.

why.T3-006: The raiding strand is explicit calls to destroy or erase rivals' work, e.g. drawing a penis over Argentina's sun and erasing every flag but Brazil's.
why.T3-061: A distinct strand grows Brazil's own flag over Argentina's and Finland's ground rather than only erasing it.
why.T3-005: A further distinct strand rallies members to defend the flag and Bunda against the Void and Blue Corner already attacking it.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-006's gate reaches only calls to destroy or erase a rival's work; it does not carry the distinct act of growing the room's own flag over Argentina's and Finland's ground without erasing.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0254062, C0552818 and C0310081 place Brazil's flag over Argentina's or expand it over neighbours' space, satisfying T3-061's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-061; dropping it loses the territorial-enlargement strand, leaving only the destroy strand.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-006's gate covers attacks the room launches; it does not carry the room's own defence against the Void and Blue Corner attacking its flag.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0251064, C0871059 and C1291147 rally defence of the flag and Bunda against the Void, satisfying T3-005's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-005; dropping it loses the defence-against-attack strand.

why.T3-105: The item is entirely about saving and reconstructing the work as it stood through screenshots, timelapses, archives, torrents and corrected retrospectives, which is T3-105's gate, not remaking it in another medium (T3-057) or entering it in an atlas (T3-112).

why.T3-070: The pair promises and then supplies a target image for placers to reproduce, which is a template shared for placing by hand, T3-070's gate, rather than the event explained (T3-016) or the mark proposed (T3-033).

why.T3-017: Most concepts are the sub's ordinary Brazil news and politics resuming after the canvas (the wall/plants story, Doria), which is T3-017's gate of carrying on the sub's usual subject, not a new canvas (T3-054, only two concepts) or an end marker (T3-117).

why.T3-087: The bulk identifies and contests who is changing the work: denying Argentina's authorship of 7-1, blaming Brazilians, correcting false accusations and stale-state errors.
why.T3-121: A distinct strand sanctions the room's own members as traitors, naming and shunning flag-spoilers and recording a ban after an infiltration.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-087's gate stops at finding out who changed the work; it does not carry the distinct act of excluding the room's own members as traitors or banning an infiltrator.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0874941, C0552779 and C0201971 call a member a traitor and C1414136 records a ban after infiltration, satisfying T3-121's exclusion gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-121; dropping it loses the sanction-by-exclusion strand behind the accusations.

why.T3-038: Many concepts report the first build's progress and hand-labour at coordinates: started, almost formed, finishing the losango outline, asking for stars.
why.T3-021: A distinct strand is repeated cleaning, repixeling of vandalised parts and hours of maintenance of the flag, Império and avocado.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-038's gate covers building and reporting progress; it does not carry the distinct upkeep act of watching, cleaning and re-fixing the work over hours.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1156759, C0151625 and C1105832 report repainting, erasing damage and hours removing vandals, satisfying T3-021's repair/upkeep gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-021; dropping it loses the maintenance strand, leaving only first construction.

why.T3-015: Every concept gathers scattered canvas talk into one hub or stickied thread and sends other posts there, which is T3-015's gate, not removals with no pointer (T3-063) or a separate sub (T3-090).

why.T3-105: As at position 2, the concepts save and rebuild the finished record through screenshots, timelapses, archives and corrected retrospectives, satisfying T3-105's gate rather than T3-057 or T3-112.

why.T3-151: The item's headline is bargaining and swapping help with neighbours; the largest strand offers, asks and conditions help in return for help, which is T3-151's gate, but the material also satisfies T3-084, T3-011, T3-010, T3-150, T3-149 and T3-115, each with three or more concepts, so it is a bag.

why.T3-073: The item's headline is telling the canvas story: recounting vigil, invasions, battles, retreats and the final version, which is T3-073's gate, but it also satisfies T3-009, T3-031, T3-043, T3-016, T3-117 and T3-154 each with three or more concepts, so it is a bag.

why.T3-052: The passages remark on activity around the room's figures - the Americans nearby, what was being built below, the neighbouring flag torn down and the unexplained face - which is T3-052's gate of remarking on neighbouring pictures, not decoding a detail (T3-018) or settling a border (T3-010).

why.T3-009: The passages mark the room's own work as achieved - 'we did it', congratulations to the team, enjoying the result - which is T3-009's gate rather than cheering builders during the work (T3-104) or crediting makers (T3-043).

why.T3-002: Every passage calls the room's own members to come and place - to coordinates, to finish Luke, to expand him, for immediate help - which is T3-002's gate rather than coordinating templates (T3-070) or repair (T3-021).

why.T3-004: The item works out what the mark should look like in the space - a brown square on the hat, whether to add Luke, a question mark and picarat design and their endorsement - which is settling the mark's design, T3-004's gate, rather than asking for a spot (T3-020) or sharing a finished template (T3-070).

why.T3-075: The leading strand objects that r/place posts are flooding and saturating the sub and asks for a separate place or relief, which is T3-075's gate, but the item also satisfies T3-027 (script/bot fairness), T3-049 (complaint of disorder) and T3-031 (humour posts) at three or more concepts each, so it is a bag.
